utterances.text: You won't find it. I was trying to explain to -- outside that the Registrar's would be the last laptop I would approach for LiveNote because usually they are doing other work, like monitoring the documents and other stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I even say just two further points. I actually even looked at the Prosecution and said generally can anyone help me with LiveNote and I realised it wasn't appropriate or they weren't going to help me and I went to that gentleman over there. And secondly, can I just say, from where I come from, there is a code of honour and decency and professional courtesy and one doesn't make scurrilous comments about one's colleagues at the Bench without just cause.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, all right. It's finished. I'm not going to hear about this. I'm not going to hear more about this. Ms. Richardson, finished. The matter is closed. So let's bring in the witness and we continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. My apologies to you, Mr. Okanovic, for having kept you longer than we had indicated earlier on. We had a technical and procedural matter that we needed to discuss, which was of no interest -- would not have been of any interest to you. So we finished with that and we can now continue. And hopefully finish today.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I should be very brief, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Apologies from me, too, Mr. Okanovic for you being unduly delayed in coming back here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm simply going to show you a clip of video in which you may recognise that there is a segment with what appears to be a film, possibly a western, which appears briefly and then it carries on. Just to confirm that it's the same video that we saw this morning. So if we could just play that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Actually, we'll keep playing because it continues.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you recognise that as being again the footage which you were shown, in fact P316 which starts at 9.23? Do you recognise it's the footage that you shot?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's just to say that that is Exhibit -- that's P428. Just for Your Honour's benefit so it's clear where that comes from, unless the Prosecution contests that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just one question. This 428 and 316, were they originally one video or two separate videos? Because -- I think it's the Prosecution that can help us on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. Apparently this, the first portion of this video was seized from one individual or taken from one particular institution. The portion that I showed yesterday was taken from -- was taken from another individual who has been a witness in this case. So it appears as though that the video was made - and perhaps the witness can give us more information about that - the video was made and there were copies, evidently, by various people made of his video which is why it ended up in different hands which is -- which also explains why we received them from different individuals at different times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Okanovic, you heard my question and you also heard the explanation forthcoming from Ms. Richardson. What's your version of -- on this? Was this originally one video recording which has ended up in bits and pieces in the hands of several persons? What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know. I don't have the original. I thought my children had erased it. However, somebody evidently took it from me without my knowledge, and what happened to it, I really don't know. I do not have the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that part, that very short clip, one second maximum, two seconds, from a film, which seems to be a western or something like that it was suggested. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No but I can tell you how it's possible. It's a small VHS tape and someone might have recorded something on it previously, and then -- if you interrupt the filming and there is a short break, and so the previous recording is left there. I have no other explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And you don't remember that film on the reel, on the tape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We won't go into it here, but we do have chain of custody details for P316 and P428 and we also have a Rule 68 issue as far as that's concerned. But I won't go into that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, I don't think we should go into that in the presence of the witness in any case. Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now on a different subject you were asked on Friday about a radio conversation in which the husband of a lady who had gone missing in Bjelovac came to you and you referred to conversations you had with someone who used the code name Gazda. Do you recall that, giving that evidence? Sorry, you do need to give a verbal answer.

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [Realtime transcript read in error: "Nerpgs nerpgs"]

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Firstly whether Gazda was in fact Naser Oric, that was an assumption that you and perhaps others made; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters can't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's clear this. Witness, when you answer, please try to -- yes exactly. To be as near the microphone as possible. And I would just for the record point out that his answer to the previous question, not to the last question, when it was pointed out to him that he needs to give a verbal answer, page 49, line 5. As his answer, on page -- on line 6, we have "nerpgs nerpgs" which I don't know what it means but I definitely heard him say DA, as I heard him say DA also in reply to the last question. In order to avoid any possibility of having -- being mistaken in this I would suggest that you put the question again, Mr. Jones, or I can read out the question to the witness myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine. I can deal with it briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You were asked, Mr. Okanovic, firstly whether Gazda was in fact Naser Oric that was an assumption that you and perhaps others made. Is that correct? And I heard you say DA, reply DA. Did you reply DA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: An assumption, but something you didn't know for sure?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It was put to you by the Prosecution that you believed Gazda was Naser Oric. I'd suggest that's not the way to put it. It was at most a working hypothesis, wasn't it, that perhaps he was Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be right to say that the identity of Gazda wasn't particularly important to you on your side because he was simply a point of contact on the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was quite obvious that this was an important person.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You never heard Gazda refer to himself as Naser or Naser Oric, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Isn't it right also that you heard people on the radio say on one or more occasions, you're Naser or you're Naser Oric, but he never confirmed that? Gazda never confirmed it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Finally, I think this is clear but you didn't know Naser Oric before the war, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And on the subject of people you knew before the war, didn't you know at least one other Naser, Naser Sulejmanovic who worked with you at the tile factory, Kaolin, in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you know that he was -- did you know that he was a radio operator in Srebrenica during the war?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you know he was a radio ham or had some sort of activity involving radios?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think he was a ham radio operator.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, in terms of contacting Gazda, on this occasion, it was essentially missing person query, wasn't it? Someone was missing and you were seeking information as to where she was. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think you told us that that sort of a query was something which was out on the radio the whole time because families had been split up and they were trying to find each other.

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But here the issue was whether the woman had jumped into the Drina or whether she had been captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you accept that you didn't contact him because you knew him to be in charge of anything in particular, he was a contact albeit an important one, on the Muslim side who you thought might be able to help?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the question. He was an important person over there, a person introducing himself as Gazda was the most important person on the other side. So he was the only person you have to communicate with about anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It was really this: That you didn't know what if any competencies Gazda had, did you? You don't know what he was in charge of or anything. He was an important contact on the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, of course this conversation took place 13 years ago. Would it be correct that you don't remember the exact words that were used by you or Gazda in discussing the fate of this woman?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember word for word.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The husband -- I don't know if you recall the name of the husband now, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Was he a friend of yours before he came and asked to use your radio or asked to be put in touch through the radio? Sorry, you need to give a verbal answer. You didn't know this gentleman beforehand?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't. I certainly didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And the husband didn't indicate any desire to try and speak to Gazda on the radio, did he? He didn't say let me speak to him or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me about a great many details. All I can say is I don't remember. He may have; he may not have. I can neither confirm nor deny.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He was staying at your house, I believe, at the time, and you said that he was by the radio the whole time. As far as you were concerned, was he free to use the radio himself directly to speak on the radio?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was free to use the radio, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You never told him, "Don't touch the radio, that's mine." He was free to use it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Why would I? It's very simple. You just push a button and you start speaking. It's nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. And I think you told us that the gist of the conversation was that -- with Gazda was that this woman hadn't been captured as a prisoner but rather evacuated from a situation of danger and that she would be returned to her own people, that that's what Gazda told you? Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was obvious that she had been captured. If she had been evacuated, she would have been returned a mere several days later. So I think the question is strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I was actually referring to what Gazda said to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you did, but you also asked him would you accept that? So in answering the way he did, I can understand him perfectly well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I can rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You either rephrase it or --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Was the gist of what Gazda said that he had evacuated -- or not he, but that she had been evacuated for her safety and would be returned?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what he said. I only know he said she was doing fine, that she was with them, and that there would be no problems. But I can't recall any specific details of the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you learnt after her release, didn't you, that she had been kept in a private house in Srebrenica, not in any sort of prison?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what she said.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I know you don't remember the details of this conversation, but it's right, isn't it, that the -- what was said by Gazda was perfectly correct, he didn't say anything menacing or unpleasant or inflammatory?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't say that. In this particular communication, he was very correct and for the most part the other people were correct too.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Some final questions just about radio equipment. You told us about the walkie-talkie which you had. You described how it didn't have much of a range particularly in mountainous terrain. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And in fact the whole terrain around Srebrenica is famously hilly and mountainous, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but if I may just add something. If this device is used from a hill top, then the range is quite large. If you speak from a depression, from a valley, if you use the UKV range, then the range is not very large because the UKV requires a certain degree of optical visibility. To keep things simple, if you use it from a hill top, then the range is quite large. If you use it from a depression or a valley, it's in fact quite small.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And these villages we have been discussing, Bjelovac, Sikiric, Pirici, they are all in a valley, aren't they? The Drina valley.

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Separated by Srebrenica by hills?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now you mentioned that if you had a relay you could overcome this difficulty in some ways and that you could, I suppose, effectively transmit to the relay and then the relay could send the message on. It's a technical matter, firstly.

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are you aware that the relays on the tops of the hills in that area, the Srebrenica area, were destroyed by the Serbs at the start of the war? Is that something you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about the TV relay stations, but both sides built their own temporary relays. There were a number of those but I'm not sure about their positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You can't confirm whether there were any of those in the Srebrenica area in 1992, any improvised relays on the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you also said that the walkie-talkie, its range could be increased if an aerial was fixed to it instead of the aerial which it comes with. Isn't it right that if that's done then it essentially has to be kept stationary at a location because it's a large aerial so you can't walk around with it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And as far as that antenna is concerned, that is something which wouldn't be easy to come by, would it, during the war or which wasn't easy to come by, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You made it yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Jones. Is there re-examination, Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mr. Okanovic, you testified that you knew Naser Sulejmanovic prior to the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: At any point during the time that you overheard communication with Gazda and any time that you spoke to him, were you under the impression that that's the Naser you were speaking with?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which Naser are you now referring to, Sulejmanovic or Oric?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question. Was Gazda, as far as you were aware, was that Naser Sulejmanovic who you worked with?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not. I knew this person well, and I was his immediate superior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard his voice on any of the radio frequencies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would just like to ask you a few questions with respect to the transcript that you read during the time that we were watching the video and certain portions of it that -- or all of it, actually, you confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: If I could ask the usher's assistance in handing the B/C/S version of the transcript to the witness so that I can put just a few questions to him. 271, Prosecution -- Defence Exhibit, excuse me, 271.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: If you look at the portion which -- the portion of the conversation occurs at -- let's begin with 022, the first voice. "Are you heading towards Bjelovac," of course I'm reading from the English version. 025 says the second voice says, "We are stopped we have stopped we cannot go forward we need help urgently." Were you under the impression at the time when you overheard this discussion on the radio that these individuals were in fact in Sikiric or in Bjelovac at 8.43, which is the time that the videotape was made?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't comment on that. I really don't know where they were stopped. This was something you heard on the radio. So -- I don't think I could possibly comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And just to confirm, I'd like to point you to another portion of the transcript at 0043. And you asked about the bombs being dropped and whether or not this conversation had -- was in any way connected with that. At 043 it says, "You heard the precise coordinates the hell. Screw it take the rest there if it is there look at the map which are the coordinates." So it means Pirici, Bjelovacka Rijeka. Now as far as you were aware, these are areas outside of the village of Sikiric?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And further down, well certainly I'll -- I'll rephrase the question. With respect to where you saw the bombs being or falling, does this -- is this consistent with where -- the areas that you saw the bombs falling?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I object to that question. Really, what the witness should be asked is whether he recalls where bombs fell. To talk about what's consistent with this transcript which already he said he can't comment on is -- I mean it's speculative. It leads nowhere. Anything is consistent, conceivably with bombs dropping there but they may have also dropped on Sikiric. So he should be asked really where he saw bombs dropping and then we'll get there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that's perfectly in order. I think first you would need to ask the witness whether he can be specific or more specific.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. I can pose the question in a different manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mr. Okanovic, whether you saw the bombs being dropped as you were videotaping the plane, the planes, were you able to determine where it was that those bombs fell?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They fell in different places. Some fell into the River Drina. Some fell on the village further down, and some fell in the hills. The area covered is a bit too large to be more specific about where each of the bombs fell.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: When you said they fell on the village further down, do you mean it fell on the houses themselves or in the vicinity of the houses or further down from the actual houses?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He should just be asked what does he mean by further down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Answer the question, please. And can you be specific. You just said that -- in describing where you saw the bombs falling, you said "on the village further down." Did you actually see bombs falling on houses or in the vicinity of houses, or further -- the question was further down or -- anyway, I think it's self-explanatory or further away from the actual houses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only thing that I saw clearly were bombs falling in the hills above the houses. Above Sikiric. Most of the bombs fell there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Is the witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Mr. Okanovic, have you completed your answer?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Judge Brydensholt do you have any questions? Judge Eser has some questions for you, Mr. Okanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Mr. Okanovic, with regard to the village, which village did you mean? I think we heard from you that Bjelovac consisted of different parts and one part was Sikiric. Now, when you spoke of village, which part of Bjelovac did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to what? What exactly do you mean? What's the reference to Sikiric about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: We were speaking, or you have been asked where the bombs fell, and you talked about a village. Now, I'm not quite clear what you mean with village because Bjelovac, as you have told, consisted or was composed of the centre of Bjelovac and some other places, hamlets, south of Bjelovac and north of Bjelovac. Now, when you spoke of village, which part did you mean?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sikiric, Sikiric. Yes, that part. There was fire there, and then the hill above that village is where most of the bombs fell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: When you had testified that there was shooting going on, was this shooting also only in Sikiric or also in other parts of Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't pinpoint the exact location. The sound was coming from across the Drina but I can't tell where from exactly, and I don't think I should be speculating. It was a very narrow angle of vision, too narrow for me to tell precisely where it was coming from but I think some of the fighting occurred in Sikiric but that's only my assumption. Although there is reference here to Bjelovac and to Kunjarac but that's further down. I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: You testified that Bjelovac was a mixed village, Muslims and Serbs. Does it mean that the mixture was within this hamlets or have there been certain areas which have been mainly Serbs and others which have been mainly Muslim and others which have been both? Was -- I hope you got my question.

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did get your question, but I don't know where they were respectively, but it was all mixed. This whole area next to the river Drina was mixed. Muslim settlements prevailed but then there were Serb settlements too but I'd be hard put to say anything more definite about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Judge Eser. I have got two short questions a part of which I think we have already dealt with but I just want to make sure of something. Whenever you had radio contact, radio conversation, with this Gazda that you mentioned, was it always the same voice that you heard at the other end?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And I -- thank you. And you also gave us to understand last Friday, in particular, that you also intercepted or you heard conversations, radio conversations, between this Gazda and others. The Gazda that you heard in conversation, in radio conversation with others, was it also the same person, the same voice, or not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the same person. Same voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Same voice, yes. And throughout this period, I think you may have answered this question, but throughout this period, did you ever come across any other radio conversation that you overheard in which someone else was referred to or he referred himself to as Gazda?

utterances.speaker: MILOS OKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was always the same voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So that brings us to an end -- or brings your testimony to an end, not us, we've still got a lot of work to do. Mr. Okanovic, on behalf of Judge Brydensholt, Judge Eser and myself of course, but also on behalf of the Tribunal in general, I would like to thank you for having come over to give testimony in this case against Naser Oric. You will now be assisted by our staff, who will help you return back home at the earliest opportunity, and you should not encounter any problems there. On behalf of everyone present also, I should like to wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, the position is we need to adjourn now. Witness number 45, I don't think he enjoys any protective measures but I would rather not mention the name. I take it that he has arrived? And that he's being briefed -- or not briefed, proofed?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And that you still need tomorrow to finish the proofing?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that he will testify, start his testimony, on Wednesday, in other words.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Anything else before we adjourn?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, so tomorrow we will not be sitting because of the proofing of this witness and we will reconvene on Wednesday in the afternoon. I think it's this same courtroom. All right. Thanks a lot. See you on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: be reconvened on Wednesday, 11 May, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
